findings.summary: plain_words loops forever on any title that contains the word 'implementation', which hangs the whole site build.
findings.evidence: Found by reading the code; not run, because I may not change files to add a test. jargon() pushes (rung.as_str(), rung.as_str().replace('-', " ")) for every rung. For Ladder::Implementation, as_str() is "implementation" (crates/athena-data/src/roles.rs:46), so the pair is ("implementation", "implementation"). plain_words runs `while let Some(start) = find_word(&out, &word)` and swaps in the same word (upper_first keeps the capital), so find_word matches again at the same offset forever. Brief::new calls plain_words on every proposal title, and render calls Brief::new, so one Steward title such as 'Move implementation notes into docs' would hang `cargo run -p xtask -- site` and the Pages job. No test uses a title containing that word. Fix: skip pairs whose replacement equals the word, or search again only after the inserted text. Separately, drop 'implementation' from the ban, since it is an ordinary English word.

findings.summary: Soundness: the verb-first test uses a list of words that are often nouns, so many problem titles become garbled questions.
findings.evidence: VERBS includes record, list, check, name, log, tag, cap, set, end, count, open, report, pin, cut, stage, change and block, and 'move' appears twice. A problem title like 'Check results are stale' or 'Record files fail to parse' gives 'Should Athena check results are stale, and so change the code, tests or docs?', which is ungrammatical and claims a change the record does not hold. This is the 'matches common words' heuristic the brief warns about. A simpler, more honest alternative: always show the title verbatim as what the record says, and ask one honest question about it. The real fix is to store the Steward's proposed change or request text, which ProposedChange.request already holds, on the work item. That is out of scope here and should be named as a follow-up.

findings.summary: Soundness: replacing jargon word by word produces nonsense titles, and the test locks one in as the expected output.
findings.evidence: The test asserts that 'Stop the Steward job from missing a blind spot in a commit path?' is shown as 'stop the Helper task from missing a gap in a saved change file'. That text is meaningless to the owner and capitalises 'Helper' mid-sentence. Every role name maps to 'helper', so titles that tell roles apart lose that meaning. 'file path' becomes 'file file'. The approach hides jargon from check() instead of making the card clear to the owner. Alternative: refuse such titles and list them as not shown, or fix the wording where titles are made (the Steward's plain_boundary_text), as the reading's root-cause default asks.

findings.summary: The question and outcome lines are still a fixed template around the title.
findings.evidence: Question = 'Should Athena ' + title + ', and so change ' + one of 5 rung areas + '?'. The 'If no' line is 'Athena does not ' + title. These lines differ per proposal only because the title differs. That passes criterion 1 literally, but adds little for the owner beyond the earlier prefix-only question. The CHANGELOG correctly names the missing record fields as still open.

summary: This change does not pass yet. One bug can hang the whole site build, and I found it by reading the code, not by running it. A proposal title containing the word "implementation" makes the title-rewording loop in xtask/src/decisions.rs run forever. That word is one of the internal words the rewording replaces, but it is replaced with itself, so the loop keeps finding it. One such Steward title would hang `cargo run -p xtask -- site` and the Pages job. No test covers it, and I didn't add one because I may not change files. Apart from that, all seven acceptance criteria are met. The 11 decision-page tests pass when I run them, and Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. Each card leads with a yes/no question, "If yes", "If no", a cost-and-risk line and a "Who decides" line, and the evidence sits in a closed details block. Cards above the raising role's limit say "you must decide", and no card recommends. Only the four expected files changed. There are also two major soundness problems. First, a title counts as a change if its first word is on a list of verbs, but many of them are also common nouns (record, check, list, name, log). A problem title like "Check results are stale" becomes the garbled question "Should Athena check results are stale…?". Second, internal words are swapped one at a time, which produces nonsense titles; the test expects "stop the Helper task from missing a gap in a saved change file". The better fix is to store the Steward's proposed change text on the work item, which this change's CHANGELOG entry already names as still open, or to refuse such titles instead of rewording them.
